messages:
Maria H: Quick proposal — I want to land a compact route-metadata + quota migration for console telemetry.
Maria H: TL;DR: denormalize a small set of route fields into the telemetry envelope (route_name, tier, org_alias), add a lightweight route_quota table for fast per-route quota checks, and run dual-write for 6 weeks before cutting reads.
Maria H: Goals: 1) cut dashboard query tails, 2) avoid huge JOINs at read time, 3) preserve backfill/replay safety for analytics.
Jon R: Can you sketch the read patterns we need to optimize? e.g., console queries that currently join routes -> events -> quotas.
Maria H: Good call. Primary patterns:
Maria H:  - per-route daily usage (time-bucketed) for quota widgets
Maria H:  - top-N routes by latency/errors in last 1h (real-time dashboard)
Maria H:  - historical audits that join route metadata + full event envelope (rare)
Sara L: Dashboard perf pain is mostly the time-bucketed per-route query. We do GROUP BY route, route_name currently comes from routes table joined by route_id.
Jon R: If we denormalize route_name and tier into the envelope we can avoid that join on the hot path.
Jon R: Example read today:
Jon R: ```sql
Jon R: SELECT r.name, date_trunc('hour', e.ts) as hr, count(*)
Jon R: FROM events e
Jon R: JOIN routes r ON r.id = e.route_id
Jon R: WHERE e.ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'
Jon R: GROUP BY r.name, hr
Jon R: ORDER BY hr DESC;
Jon R: ```
Sara L: What's the plan for schema compatibility? I don't want console crashes if old envelopes exist.
Maria H: Proposal for compatibility:
Maria H: 1) Add envelope.route_meta JSONB and envelope.route_name/tier as top-level nullable columns (text, text). 2) Console/queries prefer the top-level column if present, else fallback to JSONB, else join routes.
Maria H: 3) Dual-write at ingest: write old envelope + new route_meta + populate new columns. 4) Backfill job to fill columns for historical rows.
Sara L: That seems safe. Concern: backfill can saturate read replicas. We'll need rate-limit and chunking.
Jon R: For the route_quota table — shape?
Jon R: ```sql
Jon R: CREATE TABLE route_quota (
Jon R:   route_id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
Jon R:   daily_limit bigint,
Jon R:   window_seconds int,
Jon R:   updated_at timestamptz
Jon R: );
Jon R: CREATE INDEX ON route_quota (updated_at);
Jon R: ```
Sara L: We should avoid making the quota check require a cross-shard join for Dedicated customers. Keep route_quota small and cacheable (in-memory layer).
Maria H: Agreed — plan: route_quota is the single source for current limits; runtime will read it from the config cache (populated from DB). Console dashboards will read paired time-series from events (denormalized) + route_quota for limit bar.
TelemetryBot: CI: lint/telemetry-schema → INFO: new field envelope.route_meta added, no invalidations. :white_check_mark:
Jon R: Backfill approach suggestion: streaming job that reads events in ts order, writes new columns in batches of 5k rows with small transactions, track a safepoint table for progress.
Jon R: Also add a boolean column migrated_route_meta boolean DEFAULT false so we can easily detect partial work.
Sara L: We should also add partial indexes for the common query shapes:
Sara L: - index on (route_name, date_trunc('hour', ts)) using function index or materialized hourly buckets
Sara L: - index on (route_id, ts DESC) for recent lookups
Maria H: +1. We'll prototype an hourly_materialized view for the heavy widget and populate it from the new columns — that would reduce tail spikes.
Maria H: Rollout UX: console should show a short migration banner during the first 2 weeks of the backfill with a link to telemetry status. Add a feature flag to toggle 'prefer_denorm_route_meta'.
Sara L: Ops checklist: rate-limit backfill, monitor replica lag, have quick rollback (turn off prefer_denorm flag), and run queries in read-only shadow mode first.
Jon R: One more API debate: denorm fields vs storing everything in JSONB. My vote: keep a small set of indexed top-level columns (route_name, tier) and put the rest in JSONB to keep flexibility.
Maria H: Agreed. Index the columns we query frequently; keep JSONB for rare fields. Also add a schema_version tag to the envelope for future migrations.
TelemetryBot: Note: audit log will record all schema_version bumps and backfill start/stop events.
Sara L: Anything else for security/compliance? route_name could contain PII if teams misuse it. We should normalise/whitelist route_name patterns and add a sanitizer in ingest.
Maria H: Good catch. Add sanitizer step before denorm write and record original route_id for audit. We'll add KMS-backed avatars for sensitive configs if needed.
Jon R: OK — I can drive the migration job and a canary backfill for a single org next week. Will open PR with the DDL + backfill controller.
Maria H: Thanks — I'll draft the feature flag + console banner copy and post infra requirements.
Sara L: :eyes: Thanks, team.
TelemetryBot: Action: created ticket TI-4523 for migration runbook and TI-4524 for backfill controller.
